harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented sudo command logging on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, which has ansible-core installed). The playbook drops /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging setting `Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"`, `Defaults log_year`, `Defaults log_host`, and `Defaults !syslog`, and pre-creates the log file with 0600 root:root permissions. This makes sudo write every command (with user, host, timestamp, PWD, and COMMAND) directly to the dedicated file while suppressing sudo's normal syslog/authpriv output, keeping entries out of the general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified functionally with a real sudo invocation from a temporary test user, confirmed idempotence on replay, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for both node1 and node2, proving the configuration and log data survive a reboot and that sudo logging continues to work afterward with no new /var/log/secure entries.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (AlmaLinux9) and node2 (Ubuntu24.04, has ansible-core) to identify node2 as the Ansible control node
Wired root SSH access node2->node1 using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY
Captured baseline: no /var/log/sudo-commands.log, empty /etc/sudoers.d, /var/log/secure at 29 lines
Wrote Ansible playbook /root/ansible/sudo-logging/sudo-logging.yml and inventory.ini on node2
Ran playbook against node1 (override -u root --private-key id_ed25519 due to unrelated stale ansible.cfg defaults); succeeded, then re-ran to confirm idempotence (ok=3,changed=0)
Verified sudoers syntax with visudo -cf on node1

Created temporary test user sudologtest, ran two sudo commands as that user, confirmed entries with timestamp/user/command appeared in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and /var/log/secure gained zero sudo-related lines
Cleaned up test user and its temporary NOPASSWD sudoers drop-in
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baselines for both node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded ack), polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed
Verified sudoers file, log file, and log contents persisted after node1 reboot; ran a fresh live sudo command post-reboot confirming continued correct behavior with no growth in /var/log/secure
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed
Verified node2 control-node functionality recovered by re-running the playbook against node1 successfully (idempotent, ok=3,changed=0)

evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime, service status, and config file state on both nodes before restart

evidence.summary: Reboot command acked before disconnect; node briefly unreachable; boot_id changed from 67f3a44b... to d8e16601...

evidence.summary: Reboot command acked before disconnect; boot_id changed from 416c5cf5... to aa842e42..., uptime reset to later boot time
